headline: HOMEBODY gets the cruel word on glass — hold the A button
lede: The pad had compliments but no insults: court commands lived on keyboard C/X only. Now one thumb does both moods — tap A for the kind word, hold it two-thirds of a second and the insult flies mid-press, with a heat arc charging over the target's head.

notes.text: HOMEBODY thumb court shipped (PR #2173, issue #2171 — the never-dry pick, the shelf's weakest title): press-duration on A replaces the missing third pad button, on the same bond laws, cooldown and grudge rules as the keys. 17 new peoplecheck gates (228/0), the harness proven to catch a double-spend mutant, and a real-Chrome drive proves the heat tell pixel-for-pixel.

STRIDELINE (PR #2161, #2147) re-verified and repaired — a stray STATE.md commit on the branch made it CONFLICTING; rebased clean onto main, horsecheck 32/32, static green. The low-poly gallop is one green-nightly away.

Three PRs now sit green and merge-ready (#2166 audio crash-guard, #2161 horse demo, #2173 thumb court). Main's freeze is one Jon decision deep: jonq #2168 (papersplay ink floors re-pinned to CI calibration, default A, deadline Nov 14 22:22Z) — the gates in question have never run green on CI's software Chrome.

Playwright trap found the hard way: waitForFunction's options are the THIRD argument — pass {timeout} second and it is silently swallowed as a page-function arg while your timeout quietly defaults to 60 seconds.
